title.narrative: RMI Enhancing Fiscal Management and Building Disaster and Climate Resilience DPO with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Enhancing Fiscal Management and Building Disaster and Climate Resilience Development Policy Operation with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option for Marshall Islands are to: (i) enhance fiscal management; and (ii) build disaster and climate resilience. Pillar 1 focuses on the establishment of financial management processes and procurement practices for sound fiscal management and spending efficiency. Pillar 2 supports a suit of actions to prepare for and respond to climate change and disasters. The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) national strategic plan 2020-30 (NSP) outlines the long-term development strategy. The objective of the NSP is to attain sustainable, equitable, and measurable development that reflects the priorities and cultural values. Developed through extensive consultation, the NSP is divided into five main pillars including (i) social and culture; (ii) environment, climate change, and resilience; (iii) infrastructure; (iv), economic development; and (v) governance.

title.narrative: 1. The percentage of public sector budget preparation captured in Financial Management Information System (FMIS).

comment.narrative: The current FMIS has been in use since 1 October 2023. The annual budget for government ministries and departments is captured in the FMIS. These are prepared by line ministries and entered into the FMIS centrally by MOFBPS. The FMIS functionality is in the process of being decentralized to line ministries and FMIS configurations are underway to simplify budget data entry. Five line ministries are planned to enter budget proposals through the system by September 2026, and all line ministries by September 2027.

title.narrative: 5. Number of people with enhanced resilience to climate risks.

comment.narrative: The seawall in Ebeye, funded by the Pacific Resilience Program II – RMI Project (P160096), is expected to be completed by July 2026 and will protect 8,400 residents in Ebeye. Construction for the seawall in Majuro, adjacent the Marshall Islands High School and funded by the RMI Urban Resilience Project (P177124), commenced in January 2026 and is expected to be completed in July 2028, beyond the closing date of this project, and will protect at least 1,400 people. The target is on track to be met by project closing.

title.narrative: 2. Annual public procurement spending processed via e-procurement system.

comment.narrative: The Public Financial Management II project (P510280) is the primary vehicle for the e-procurement system. This results indicator is advancing in line with reform sequencing: an Electronic Government Procurement (E-GP) assessment launched in April 2026 is determining a fit-for-purpose system compatible with the Financial Management Information System (FMIS), with uptake toward the 30 percent FY27 target expected thereafter.

title.narrative: 3. The percentage of atolls with approved disaster plans including climate adaptation measures.

comment.narrative: A National Disaster Management Plan, incorporating guidance for the incorporation of climate adpatation measures in atoll-level disaster plans is expected to be finalized by May 2026, under the Pacific Resilience Program II – RMI Project (P160096). While disaster plans for all 22 inhabited atolls have been approved, the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) is committed to updating these plans to incorporate climate adpatation measures. The Additional Financing to the RMI Urban Resilience Project (P177124) is supporting the update of ten disaster management plans, expected to be completed by mid-2028. The end target of 6 updated plans is likely to be met by the closing date of this operation but continued Bank team support is needed to ensure the target is met timely.

title.narrative: 6. The percentage of new national government buildings with a building permit issued.

comment.narrative: The Nitijela (Parliament) approved the National Building Code Act 2025 on September 19, 2025, and the Building Safety and Regulation Division (BSR) of the Ministry of Public Works, Infrastructure and Utilities (MPWIU) continued to make progress on raising awareness of the National Building Code (NBC). No additional building permit applications for national government buildings have been submitted to the BSR since the first building permit was approved in 2025 in April 2025 for a resilient national government facility, the construction of which is ongoing and being funded under the RMI Urban Resilience Project (RMI URP, P177124). BSR is continuing internal discussions to arrange for a special account to receive building permit fees but additional building regulations may be needed. The Bank team is continuing its technical assistance program (funded by the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery) with BSR.

title.narrative: 4. The percentage of local government disaster committees comprising over 45 percent women.

comment.narrative: A National Disaster Management Plan, incorporating guidance for the incorporation of women's composition in local government disaster committees, is expected to be finalized by May 2026, under the Pacific Resilience Program II – RMI Project (P160096). The baseline of 30 percent has not yet changed but the National Disaster Management Office is committed to increasing women's participation once the national plan is approved.

comment.narrative: A National Disaster Management Plan, incorporating guidance for the incorporation of women's composition in local government disaster committees, is expected to be finalized by May 2026, under the Pacific Resilience Program II – RMI Project (P160096). The baseline of 30 percent has not yet changed but the National Disaster Management Office is committed to increasing women's participation once the national plan is approved.
